text:
Alicia C.: quick PSA — running AWQ weight-only quant on latest serving runtime and seeing a 12-18% tail perf regression on long sequences vs current fp32 path. attaching quick numbers below, need ideas.
Samir: can you paste the profiler output? regression compute-bound or memory/packing overhead?
Alicia C.: paste: ```
# microbench gpt-small, seq=1024, batch=1
fp32: kernel=18.9ms, memcpy=1.1ms, total=20.0ms
awq group=32 packed: pack=4.8ms, kernel(int8)=17.2ms, unpack=1.4ms, total=23.4ms
delta +3.4ms (~17%) — p95 spikes on KV reloads
```
perf-bot: nightly bench summary: awq-group32 pack-time median 4.8ms, pack stddev 1.1ms; group64 pack-time median 6.9ms but kernel speedup ~10% for small batches.
Anya: interesting — sounds like packing overhead + KV cache churn. did you isolate hot path? i.e., is pack done per-request or cached per-model-version?
Alicia C.: pack currently happens lazily per warmed allocator region; we only cache raw FP weights. when KV cache hits with different prefix lengths we re-pack per-request because we materialize per-sequence attention masks. leads to repetitive pack/unpack for streaming workloads.
Ron: for kernel selection: we should prefer the int8-matmul kernel only when seq < threshold or when batch>1; otherwise the packing amortization is bad. propose heuristic: if estimated pack_cost / (tokens * kernel_speedup) > 0.25 then route to fp32 or group64.
Anya: also try changing group-size. AWQ group=16/32/64 tradeoffs: smaller groups -> better quality, smaller packed size but higher packing ops per weight. bigger groups -> faster kernels but worse quant error. do we have quant-error vs perf table?
Alicia C.: quick eval (lm-eval tiny set): ```
AWQ g16 -> ppl=12.2, pack=3.9ms, kernel=17.8ms, total=21.7ms
AWQ g32 -> ppl=12.6, pack=4.8ms, kernel=17.2ms, total=23.4ms
AWQ g64 -> ppl=13.5, pack=6.9ms, kernel=15.4ms, total=22.3ms
FP32   -> ppl=12.0, total=20.0ms
```
Alicia C.: so g64 narrows kernel time but pack cost grows; quality drift noticeable at g64 on some prompts.
Infra Bot: FYI we can store pre-packed weights in shared memory per model-version (disk cache + mmap) to avoid repacking on every cold KV access. downside: storage cost and increased deploy-time.
Samir: what about doing partial packing: only pack the active projection blocks used by recent prefixes, lazy background pack for rest? reduces tail pack latency.
Ron: sounds good. also consider changing batching heuristics: for streaming single-token requests prefer cached-packed path; for long single-seq generation, prepack full model ahead of decode start. can use decoder-cost estimator to decide.
Anya: calibration notes: we saw calibration sample size/representativeness impacts latency/quality tradeoff. AWQ tiny calibration (50 samples) gives better perf but more scatter in perplexity vs GPTQ per-group cal. need to standardize calibration set per-customer workload.
Alicia C.: QA: small calibration set improved quant scales for common tokens but caused regressions on rare tokens -> observed hallucination increase on a couple internal tests. g32 seemed safest default.
perf-bot: canary results: route=awq-g32-packed => p50 latency - +8%, p95 +16%, quality metric delta (R1) -0.8pts on guard set.
Samir: plan suggestion: 1) implement prepacked artifact storage for Dedicated; 2) add heuristic in router to pick fp32 path when estimated amortization bad; 3) default AWQ group=32 with opt-in g64 for throughput-critical customers; 4) add calibration checklist and larger representative sample.
Alicia C.: action items: @Anya run 24h quality sweep on 10k prompts for g16/g32/g64, @Ron prototype router heuristic + estimator, @Infra Bot work out prepacked storage mmap perf and disk footprint estimate, @Samir help add canary metrics for p95 tokens and hallucination signals. I'll assemble a short RFC if we agree. :+1:
Ron: acked. I'll spike the pack amortization estimator this week.
Anya: I'll start the sweep and post results in this thread.
Infra Bot: noted — creating ticket INF-3241 for prepacked artifacts and storage quotas.
Alicia C.: thanks all — keep replies short, prefer numbers. we should avoid broad assumptions before the sweep. :rocket:
